The weapon was recovered during a joint operation involving personnel of the 6 Brigade Garrison of the Nigerian Army and operatives of the Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA). The operation, which reportedly took place at about 9:50pm on November 13, 2026, followed the suspect’s arrest at Technobat in Jalingo, the state capital, on October 20. Security analyst Zagazola Makama disclosed this in a post on his X handle on Sunday, stating that operatives traced the suspect’s residence to Wukari following his arrest. According to the report, a search of the residence led to the discovery and recovery of the AK-47 rifle, which was subsequently taken into military custody for further investigation and necessary action. The recovery comes amid growing concerns over the proliferation of illegal firearms and the activities of armed criminal groups in Taraba State, particularly in parts of the southern senatorial district. Speaking on efforts to tackle illegal arms trafficking and dismantle networks supplying weapons to criminal groups, a senior military officer of the 6 Brigade in Wukari, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the military was working closely with other security agencies to improve the security situation in the area. The officer said security agencies were committed to strengthening intelligence gathering and operational collaboration but cautioned that arrests must be backed by credible information and thorough investigations. “Whenever we encounter individuals in possession of illegal arms, the information is reported for appropriate action. “We are doing our best to address the situation and strengthen our operations in collaboration with other security agencies in Wukari and its environs. “When the Brigade resumed operations in the area, we met some people already on the ground. We have been working to improve the security situation, particularly by collaborating closely with other security agencies to enhance operational efficiency. “We are also committed to ensuring that the situation improves significantly. We believe that with increased collaboration and more effective operations, things will be much better than they were previously,” the officer said. The officer, however, stressed that the military would not embark on indiscriminate arrests without establishing credible grounds for action. “We cannot just go out and arrest people without proper investigations. Every case must be thoroughly investigated before any action is taken. “Even when an arrest is made, it must be based on credible information and proper investigative procedures. “We do not just apprehend people arbitrarily. There must be sufficient grounds and evidence to establish their involvement before taking further action,” he added. He urged members of the public with credible information about illegal arms dealers and their activities to report such information to his office for necessary investigation and action. Meanwhile, the military has yet to disclose the identity of the suspect or provide further details about the circumstances surrounding his arrest as of the time of filing this report. It was also unclear whether the suspect had been formally charged before a court.
